title: Data territory exemption catalog and actionable checklist
summary: Working catalog of residency exemption types, risk controls, required telemetry, and an operator checklist for approving/implementing temporary or permanent territory exceptions for private deployments.
body:
Purpose:
This is a working document for private-deployments, SRE, and legal to standardize how we evaluate, approve, and operationalize exceptions to region pinning / strict data residency requests. Focus is on pragmatic controls (timeboxed approvals, masking, auditing, routing constraints) that reduce legal and operational risk while enabling sales/CS use cases that otherwise would be blocked.

Audience:
- Solutions Engineering (customer asks)
- Oncall / Operators (implementation)
- Legal & Compliance (risk accept)
- Product (policy updates)

High-level flows (summary):
1) Customer requests an exemption (via SE or CSM). Create Jira PD-EXEMPT-<customer> and tag LEGAL/SEC.
2) Intake form (SE fills): scope of data, intended region(s) to process in, duration (temporary/permanent), business justification, compliance exemptions requested (e.g., contractual carve-out).
3) Quick triage (SRE + SE): assign risk tier (low/medium/high) using matrix below. If high -> require legal approval + exec sign-off.
4) Implementation plan (Operators): config changes (region routing override, model variant pinning), telemetry hooks, audit party, rollback plan.
5) Post-approval monitoring: 48h elevated telemetry, weekly review during the exemption window.
6) Expiry and cleanup: automated reversion at TTL + verification job run to assert routes reverted and no residual data copies.

Exemption types (catalog) - examples and typical controls:
- Temporary engineering access (debugging):
  Controls: timeboxed (max 48h), SSH/API access scoped by IP allowlist, session recording enabled, ephemeral creds, operator supervision.
  Telemetry: request logs, session replays, list of modified artifacts.
  Typical risk: moderate; acceptable for non-PII or pseudonymized payloads only.

- Contractual carve-out (customer requests processing outside home region for specific workloads):
  Controls: written contract clause, legal sign-off, region-allowlist for customer tenant, encryption-at-rest w/ customer KMS in target region, dedicated logging with restricted retention.
  Telemetry: per-tenant routing logs, KMS audit events, storage object access logs.
  Typical risk: high; requires executive + legal approval and quarterly review.

- Cross-border temporary burst (capacity overflow):
  Controls: automated policy triggers only when a defined capacity threshold is exceeded; fallback to geo-boundary awareness; customer opt-in for burst; masking of sensitive attributes if possible.
  Telemetry: capacity events, per-request residency tag, latency and cost delta.
  Typical risk: low-to-moderate if masked/opt-in.

- Operator-initiated failover (disaster scenario):
  Controls: pre-authorized playbook, predefined failover targets, immediate post-failover audit and notification to customer/Legal, preserve original residency evidence for audit.
  Telemetry: failover timeline, p99 latency shifts, data movement audit trail.
  Typical risk: depends on RTO; must be logged and reported within 24h.

Risk tiering matrix (quick):
- Low: non-sensitive payloads, ephemeral session debugging, customer explicitly opt-in, TTL <= 72h.
- Medium: encrypted but identifiable data, permanent routing change for limited workloads, third-party subprocessors in target region. Requires legal review.
- High: regulated data (health, finance), contractual residency guarantees, permanent cross-border processing. Requires legal + leadership sign-off and documented mitigation.

Required signoffs and artifacts (minimum):
- SE intake note (Jira) with scope and justification
- SRE implementation plan (config diffs / rollout plan)
- Legal memo (if medium/high) describing compliance rationale and acceptance
- Security checklist: KMS usage, network isolation, audit logging enabled
- Ops acceptance tests: route verification script, telemetry dashboards, revert script

Operator checklist (actionable; follow when implementing):
1) Confirm Jira PD-EXEMPT ticket exists and has required approvals.
2) Snapshot current routing config and save to ops repo.
3) Apply region-allowlist for tenant in staging, smoke test with synthetic traffic.
4) Enable elevated telemetry: residency-tagging, request headers capture (no raw payload retention unless approved), KMS logs.
5) Deploy config to canary subset (1-5% traffic) for 2h. Monitor errors, latency, and access logs.
6) If no regressions, ramp to requested percentage or full route.
7) Start TTL countdown; annotate ticket with expiry timestamp and scheduled revert job.
8) For temporary exemptions, run automated verification at expiry: assert no requests route to exception region, confirm no persisted artifacts remain outside approved boundaries.
9) Post-reversion: produce evidence bundle (logs + snapshots) and upload to Jira ticket; notify Legal and SE.

Telemetry & alerting (what to show on dashboards):
- Per-tenant residency tag counts (by region)
- List of recent exemption actions (who, when, reason)
- KMS access spikes correlated with exemption windows
- Failed route-attempts to pinned regions (indicates possible misconfiguration)
- Data egress/cost delta during exemption period
- Audit anomalies (unexpected IPs, large bulk downloads) -> paged alert to SRE oncall + Legal (if high severity)

Retention & evidence requirements:
- Keep exemption evidence bundle for minimum 2 years for enterprise customers under audit.
- Where legal requires longer retention, follow contract terms and central archive procedure.

Customer comms templates (short):
- Pre-approval: "We have logged your exemption request. Next steps: engineering triage and a risk review with Legal. We will follow up within 3 business days with required controls and ETA for implementation."
- Post-implementation: "Your routing change is live for the agreed scope. We will monitor for 48 hours and follow up with a summary and evidence package. If this was temporary, the route will revert on [expiry]."

Open questions / decisions needed (for leadership/legal):
- Maximum allowed duration by tier: should medium-tier temporary exceptions be capped at 90 days?
- Default masking policy: what attributes must be masked for medium-tier exemptions before approval?
- Automated enforcement: which actions should auto-revert vs require manual operator revert?
- Billing/SLAs: do we bill customers for cross-region egress during exemption or absorb cost? (Product needs guidance)

Implementation notes for infra (dev notes):
- Router config: we will support an ordered-allowlist per-tenant with TTL metadata and audit fields. Implementation PR: ops/region-router#426.
- Verification job: a lambda-run job that queries residency tags across traces and asserts zero hits to banned regions; add to cron-runner with immediate invocation at expiry.
- Audit bundle generator: small service to collect logs + KMS events + config snapshot -> gzipped artifact uploaded to secure S3 path with tenant ACL.

Appendix - quick commands / playbook snippets (operators):
- Save config snapshot: gitops repo cli: gitops snapshot create --path tenants/<id>/routes --message "pre-exempt-snapshot"
- Apply canary: infractl route apply --tenant <id> --region-allowlist eu-west-1 --canary 0.03 --note "EXEMPT PD-1234"
- Revert: infractl route revert --snapshot pre-exempt-snapshot --ticket PD-1234

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally pragmatic; we expect followups: more rigid SLA language, automation to reduce manual steps, and integration with the enrollment signing workflow for high-risk contracts.
- Prioritize adding a telemetry panel in Grafana that shows per-tenant residency exposures in the next sprint.

End of doc.
